## History and Physical

## Chief Complaint
Chest pain for 3 hours.

## History of Present Illness
68-year-old man with hypertension and hyperlipidemia who presents with substernal chest pressure that began 3 hours ago while walking to his car. Pain is pressure-like, 7/10, radiates to the left arm, associated with diaphoresis and mild shortness of breath. No prior similar episodes. Denies palpitations, syncope, orthopnea, PND, leg swelling, fever, cough.

## Past Medical History
Hypertension, hyperlipidemia, type 2 diabetes mellitus.

## Medications
- Lisinopril 10 mg daily
- Atorvastatin 40 mg nightly
- Metformin 1000 mg twice daily
- Aspirin 81 mg daily

## Allergies
NKDA.

## Social History
Former smoker, quit 10 years ago. Occasional alcohol. Works as an accountant.

## Family History
Father had MI at age 60.

## Review of Systems
Chest pain and dyspnea as above. Denies fever, cough, abdominal pain, dysuria.

## Physical Exam
Vitals: T 98.4 F, HR 92, BP 148/92, RR 18, SpO2 97% on room air.
General: Alert, mild distress from pain.
HEENT: Normocephalic, atraumatic.
CV: Tachycardic, regular rhythm, no murmurs.
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Abdomen: Soft, nontender.
Extremities: No edema.

## Labs
Labs: WBC 11.2, Hgb 14.1, Plt 220, Na 139, K 4.1, Creatinine 1.1, Glucose 168, Troponin 0.45 (H)

## Studies
EKG: ST elevations in anterior leads.
CXR: No acute cardiopulmonary process.

## Assessment
68-year-old man with acute chest pain concerning for acute coronary syndrome.

## Plan
1. Acute coronary syndrome, likely STEMI
- Cardiology consult, cath lab activation
- Aspirin, heparin per protocol
- Serial troponins and EKGs

2. Hypertension
- Monitor blood pressure, hold ACE inhibitor if hypotensive

3. Type 2 diabetes mellitus
- Fingerstick glucose monitoring, sliding scale insulin
